_doc: Hand decisions for tools/state_towns.py (re-run it after editing; never hand-edit towns.tsv). Sources: Census Gazetteer 2023 places, popest 2023 (incorporated), Gazetteer 2010 POP10 (CDPs).
_regions: First match wins. valley = the Lower Rio Grande Valley (Cameron, Hidalgo, Starr and Willacy counties: a box south of 26.8 and east of -99.3); gulf = a coastal band about 50-70 km deep from Orange and Beaumont-Port Arthur past the Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay suburbs to Corpus Christi and Kingsville (inner Houston, Victoria and Alice stay out); panhandle = the Panhandle and the South Plains north of 33.45 and west of the 100th meridian (Amarillo, Lubbock); west = west of a hand-drawn dry line (about -99.9 at the Red River, -98.9 near Brownwood, -98.6 at the Hill Country edge, west of San Antonio, -98.0 at the valley): Trans-Pecos, Permian Basin, Edwards Plateau, the Big Country and the border country (El Paso, Midland, Abilene, San Angelo, Laredo, Del Rio); east = the rest (default: DFW, Houston, Austin, San Antonio, Piney Woods, Central Texas).
_incMinPop: Texas has 1,225 incorporated places, far more than the 400-550 target, so incorporated places get a population floor per region (2023 estimate): east 6500 (the dense metros), west 800, gulf 1500, panhandle 400, valley 2000, which keeps every climate pool large enough. keepTown keeps well-known small towns below the floor (Hill Country, Fayette County, East Texas historic towns, Surfside Beach).
_cdp: CDPs only by hand (cdpMinPop is effectively off): The Woodlands and Spring (large, well-known Houston-area communities), Big Bend and Trans-Pecos places (Fort Davis, Terlingua, Study Butte, Sanderson), Hill Country (Comfort, Utopia, Canyon Lake) and coast (Port O'Connor, Matagorda, Bolivar Peninsula, Port Mansfield).
_rename: The Census name of the Reeves County seat is 'Town of Pecos city'; the city is known and signed as Pecos.
